text:
Someone wants to order the same groceries they get every week.
Reorder groceries
Get me my usual order again.
Same as last time, please.
I hope you can send the same box as last week, with the potatoes.
Can you repeat my last shop?
Order what I got before.
Could you please put in my usual grocery order for Friday, since I am out of almost everything?
Do my weekly shopping again.

A bedtime routine is a small set of things you do each night so your body knows it is time to sleep. Many people set a daily alarm so they wake up at the same time every morning. Some also run a quiet dehumidifier in the bedroom, so the air feels dry and fresh. When plans change, people talk to their phone or speaker to change things. They might say, wake me at six instead of seven, or, move my bedtime reminder to ten. Others say, no alarm on Sunday, or, push my alarm back half an hour. For a nap, they say, wake me in twenty minutes. These small changes help a person get enough rest.

Person: Text Anna.
Assistant: What would you like the message to say?
Person: Tell her I will bring a carrot cake on Sunday.
Assistant: Okay. Should I say what time you will come?
Person: Yes, but nothing fancy. Just say I will be there at noon.
Assistant: Done. I sent Anna: I will bring a carrot cake on Sunday and be there at noon.
Person: Good. Can you also burn the group photos onto a disc for me?
Assistant: I am sorry, I can not burn discs. I can send the photos to the group chat instead.
Person: Yes, please do that.

Someone wants to book a haircut.
Book a haircut.
Haircut tomorrow, please.
Can I get a trim on Friday at ten? No, make it eleven.
I need to see the barber before the shop closes on Saturday.
Put me down for a cut on Monday. Actually no, there is ice on the roads, so make it Tuesday.
My hair is healthy but too long, so please find me a time this week.
Sorry, not Thursday, I meant Wednesday afternoon.
Could you please check if the salon has a free spot after lunch and reserve it for me?

Ben was seven, and he wanted to help Grandma bake cookies. The kitchen had a small speaker on the shelf. Ben stood on a chair and said, Cookie time? The speaker understood that he wanted a cookie recipe, so it read the first step: sort the flour, the sugar and the butter on the counter. Outside, the traffic was loud, and Ben did not hear the next part. He said, Say again. The assistant read the step more slowly. Then Ben asked how long the cookies bake. The assistant said twelve minutes and set a timer for twelve minutes. While they waited, Ben sorted the chocolate chips by size, and Grandma laughed.

Someone wants to move money from checking to savings.
Move fifty dollars to savings.
Put half of my paycheck into savings.
I want less in checking and more in savings before winter.
Please stir some life into my savings and move double the usual amount.
Move my loose cash, anything over five hundred, into savings.
Send a bit more to savings this month than last month.
Could you please transfer a little extra to my savings account, because I want to be ready for the holidays?
Savings, one hundred, now.

Priya looked at the clock. Her guests would arrive in twenty-five minutes, and the floor was covered in crumbs and the pieces of a puzzle she had not finished. She said to her phone, Clean the living room, quick, my friends are coming. The assistant understood that she wanted the robot vacuum to start in the living room only, so it did that and said the cleaning would take about fifteen minutes. Priya hurried to pick up the puzzle pieces so the robot would not swallow them. From the kitchen came the delicious smell of her soup. When she picked up the last piece, she asked the assistant to tell her when the robot was done. It said it would, and it did, with three minutes to spare.

Grandpa Leo sat at the kitchen table with his tea, and a gray cat slept on his lap. He stirred the tea slowly and looked at his granddaughter's drawing on the fridge. Then he remembered his sore tooth. He said to the tablet, I need to see the dentist sometime next week, in the morning. The assistant understood that he wanted a dentist visit early next week. It checked the dentist's open times and found Tuesday at ten. Leo asked if there was anything earlier. The assistant said the first free time was nine-thirty on Wednesday, so Tuesday at ten was sooner. Leo said Tuesday was fine, and the assistant booked it. It also set a reminder for twenty minutes before, so he would leave on time.

Nina got home after a long night shift. The morning was humid, and her shirt stuck to her back. A magazine lay on the mat, and a bird began to tweet in the tree. At the front door she stopped. She could not remember if she had locked it when she left the evening before. She was too tired to check, so she said to her phone, Check the lock. The assistant understood that she meant the front door, so it looked at the smart lock and told her the door was locked and had been since seven the evening before. Nina smiled. She said, Unlock it, and the assistant did. She went in and fell asleep within minutes.

Person: Translate good morning for my neighbor.
Assistant: Which language would you like?
Person: Not French. She speaks Portuguese. Learning it is my new hobby.
Assistant: Good morning in Portuguese is bom dia. Would you like to hear how to say it?
Person: Yes, and say it slowly. I am not very quick.
Assistant: Bom dia. Bom dia. You are doing well.
Person: You are very patient. Can you update my phone so it always shows words in Portuguese?
Assistant: I am sorry, I can not change that setting. I can save bom dia in your list of new phrases, though.
Person: Please do.

Dana's morning was busy. While she packed lunches, she said to her speaker, Remind me to pick up Sam from soccer at four. The assistant understood and set a reminder for four o'clock. Then Dana smelled toast burning and ran to the toaster. When she came back she said, Actually, make it half past three, the coach said practice ends early. The assistant changed the reminder from four to three-thirty and told her so. Dana was working from home that day and had an article to finish, so she asked for a second reminder ten minutes earlier. The assistant added it. At three-twenty her phone buzzed, and she saved her work just in time.

Music on a phone or a speaker is mostly about songs and the lists you make from them. A playlist is a set of songs played in order. People use music to wake up, to cook, or to sit under a blanket on a rainy day. They change a few things all the time. For volume they say, turn it up, a bit lower, or, mute. To skip a track they say, next song, or, skip this one. If a song is too heavy for the mood, they say, play something softer. If they want to cut a song short, they say, stop after this one. To start again, they say, play my evening playlist.

Omar drove a delivery van, and on his lunch break he parked near the river. At dawn he had left a tray of rolls rising at home, and now the dough was ready to bake. He picked up his phone and said, Excuse me, could you please start the oven at four hundred degrees now, because I will be home in twenty minutes and I want the rolls to go in as soon as I walk in the door? The assistant understood that he wanted the smart oven to warm up. It started the oven and said it would be hot in about ten minutes. Omar drove home with the windows open, and the air smelled like cut grass. When he got in, the oven was ready, and the rolls baked to a deep gold.

name: scale_recipe
does: Changes the amounts in a recipe so it makes more or fewer servings.
inputs: the recipe and how many servings you want
people say:
- Make this healthy soup for twelve instead of four.
- Write out the pancake recipe for the ten kids in my drum class.
- Cut this recipe in half, it is only me tonight.
- How much flour if I double it?
- My chili feeds six, but fifteen people are coming.
- Triple the sauce, please.

Someone wants to know how far they walked today.
How far have I gone?
Distance so far.
How many miles did I run this morning? No, sorry, I mean walk.
I wish I knew how far I got before the rain started.
Tell me my distance from the walk on the dry path by the lake.
What is my total since I left home?
Could you please tell me how far I have walked today, because I want to see if I reached five miles?
Show today's distance, not this week's.

name: pack_lunch_ideas
does: Suggests lunches that are easy to carry and stay fresh until noon.
inputs: who the lunch is for, any foods they avoid, and how much time you have
people say:
- What can I put in a lunch box that stays fresh in a hot car?
- Lunch ideas, and fast, I have to go before I blink.
- The kids eat downstairs, so nothing that needs a microwave.
- Something cold for Dad's lunch, no nuts.
- I am tired of sandwiches, give me five other ideas.

Tom had just enough money left to pay the rent, so tonight he had to cook. He took off his muddy boot by the door and opened the fridge. The kitchen was small, and he had only one pot and one pan. He said to his phone, Pasta recipe? The assistant understood that he wanted an easy recipe for pasta. It found one with tomatoes and garlic and read out the steps. Tom asked for the first step again, and the assistant said, boil water in the pot with some salt. He asked how long the pasta needed. Ten minutes, said the assistant, and it set a timer. The meal was easy, and Tom ate every bite.

Rosa came home from the night shift and dropped onto the couch. She had ordered a pair of sandals last week, and she wanted to know about them. She said to her phone, Where is my sandal order and can you leave it with my neighbor if I am asleep? The assistant understood two things: she wanted to see where the package was, and she wanted it left next door. It said the package was on a truck a few stops away and would come by noon. It then changed the delivery note to leave it with the neighbor in apartment four. Rosa asked it to zoom in on the map to see how far the truck was. It was only a few streets away, and Rosa fell asleep smiling.

Maria owned a small bookshop, and tonight was its tenth birthday party. The shelves were full of balloons, and she still had to fold fifty paper napkins. Her hands were busy, so she said to the speaker, Party music. The assistant understood that she wanted a playlist for a party, so it chose a cheerful list of songs and played it at a medium volume. Maria said, Not so loud, and it turned the music down. Later, as she cut the cake with a sharp knife, she asked for more volume because the guests were arriving. The assistant raised it, and the shop filled with music and laughter.

Jun had just moved to the city, and his building had many rules about trash. A paper on the wall used a word he did not know. He took out his phone and said, Excuse me, could you please tell me how to say recycling bin in Dutch, because I want to put my things in the right place and not upset the neighbors? The assistant understood that he wanted a translation of the words recycling bin. It said the Dutch words and spelled them slowly. Jun repeated them. Then the assistant asked if he wanted to save the phrase, and he said yes, so it saved the words in his list of new phrases. Jun carried his box of paper down to the white bin and put it in.

Every street has a few problems that neighbors share: a lost cat, a noisy party, or a meeting about the park. A neighborhood chapter helps people stay in touch. Most of the usual news comes in one weekly message. A person can change what they get. They might say, tell me about local events on Saturdays, or, mute the chat after ten at night. If a dog is lost, someone says, send a message to the whole street with a photo. If the noise is too much, people say, let the landlord know. It is easy to understand once you try it: you say what you want, and the group hears it.

Hana had a long day ahead at the office. On her way in, she said to her phone, Remind me to call the town hall at noon and to buy stamps when I go past the high street shop. The assistant understood that she wanted two reminders. It set the first one for twelve o'clock and the second one for when she left the building at five, near the shop. Hana also said the town hall reminder should ring ten minutes early, since the high building's phone lines were always busy. The assistant changed it. At ten to twelve her phone buzzed, and she made the call before lunch.

Sam moved to the city last week, and the nights were strange. A bus rumbled by at midnight, and a siren sang at two. Tired, Sam said to the speaker, Set an alarm for six tomorrow. The assistant set it. Then Sam remembered a late shift and said, No wait, make it seven. The assistant changed the alarm from six to seven and said so out loud. Sam tried to describe the noise outside and asked for something soft to cover it. The assistant played rain sounds for one hour. Sam, who had started a new diet and was hungry, drank some water and fell asleep before the first song ended.

Mr. Hale did not trust his phone much. It felt strange to talk to it. But his son was playing in a big match that day, and Mr. Hale wanted to know the score. He held the phone and said, Excuse me, could you please tell me how the Tigers are doing, because my son is playing and I could not get a ticket? The assistant understood that he wanted the score of the Tigers game. It said the Tigers were ahead, three to one, at halftime. Mr. Hale smiled. He asked it to place a note on his calendar for the next game, and the assistant did. Then he went out to his truck to drive to the stadium anyway.

A work meeting is a time when people talk about a plan. Many meetings now happen on calls. You join with a link, and you can share your screen if you need to show a page. An agenda is a short list of what will be talked about, like a new design or a store discount. People change things often. They say, mute me, I will be away from my desk for a minute, or, share my screen, or, move the meeting to three o'clock. When someone is late they say, start without me. These small requests keep a meeting smooth.

name: sort_incoming_mail
does: Tells you which letters and parcels arrived today and which are only junk.
inputs: your address and what you are expecting
people say:
- Anything important in the mail today?
- Did my box of butter cookies come yet?
- Trim the junk out of today's mail and tell me what is left.
- Is there a plain white envelope from the bank?
- Tell me when a package is at the door.

name: find_quiet_route
does: Finds a walking route that stays away from busy roads and has no stairs.
inputs: where you start, where you want to go, and what you want to avoid
people say:
- Take me to the park by a quiet way.
- I can not lift the stroller up stairs, so find a flat path.
- Go over the iron bridge, and skip the noisy main road.
- Which way to the library has the fewest cars?
- Plan my evening walk, nothing busy.

Person: Move some money to my savings.
Assistant: How much would you like to move?
Person: Not all of it. I only want to save a little for a new bicycle.
Assistant: Okay. Would two hundred be good?
Person: That is too much. Make it one hundred.
Assistant: Done. I moved one hundred from checking to savings. The total in savings is now six hundred.
Person: Good. A gentle start is fine, and I do not want any fee.
Assistant: There is no fee for moving money between your own accounts.

On Saturday morning Lena said to her speaker, When does the Lions match start? The assistant said it started at five. Lena said, No, I meant the Falcons, my son's team. The assistant checked again and said the Falcons played at six. Lena asked how much a ticket was, and it said ten euro. She remembered that her son's uniform was not clean, so she asked for a reminder to wash it before lunch. The kids always shout so loudly at games, she said with a laugh. The assistant set the reminder and one more for four-thirty, when it was time to leave.

When something in the house breaks, you can fix it yourself or ask for help. A repair shop or a handyman can come to your door. A filter in a heater or a fan needs to be changed every few months, so it is good to double check the date. People often have a problem upstairs, like a leaky tap, and they say, book a repair for Thursday. They change the plan by saying, make it morning, or, move it to next week. They ask, when is my filter due, or, remind me to change it in a month. Saying what is wrong and when you are free is the most helpful thing.

name: pick_wash_cycle
does: Chooses the right washing machine setting for a load of clothes.
inputs: what the clothes are made of, how dirty they are, and how long you have
people say:
- What setting for my sister's silk shirt?
- Will a hot wash shrink these jeans?
- How much does it cost to use cold water compared to warm?
- I have towels and sheets, which program is best?
- Fast wash, I need these dry by noon.

Someone wants to know when a friend's birthday is and what to give.
Date and gift for Sam?
When is Mia's birthday and what should I get her?
I always forget, so tell me the date and suggest a present.
Change the setting so you warn me a week before each birthday and give me ideas.
Is Dad's birthday this month, and is there a card I can print?
Do not let me drag my feet again: give me the date and something small to buy.
Could you please tell me when Anna's birthday is and check whether I am free that evening?

Mika was making breakfast for three kids when her phone rang with a call from work. She had no free hand, so she let it ring and said to the kitchen speaker, Make the coffee twice as strong today, and start the kettle for tea too. The assistant understood that she wanted a stronger coffee and hot water. It told the coffee machine to use a double portion and switched on the kettle. The kids zoom around the table like little planes, and one of them asked for less milk in the cereal. Mika laughed and poured half a cup. The assistant also reminded her that the monthly cleaning of the coffee machine was due on Friday.

Carl owned a shoe shop and was checking prices on his tablet. The numbers were tiny. He ate a sandwich as he worked, next to a stack of yellow price tags. He held the tablet at arm's length and said, These letters are so small, I need a magnifying glass. The assistant understood that he could not read the screen, so it made the text size bigger and asked if that was enough. Carl said a bit more. The assistant made the text larger again, and Carl nodded. Then he said the screen was too bright for the sunny shop window, and the assistant lowered the brightness.

Someone wants an email to be sent later, at a set time.
Send it tomorrow at seven.
Email Dan the painting photos at eight tomorrow morning.
Hold this message and send it at noon.
I will lie in tomorrow, so please send this email at nine for me.
Schedule my note to the nearby bakery for Monday at ten.
Do not send it now, wait until after lunch.
Could you please send this email tomorrow at seven, since people read their messages first thing?
Delay sending until tomorrow evening.

name: write_quick_reply
does: Writes a short reply to a text message in the style you prefer.
inputs: the message you got and how you want to sound
people say:
- Reply to Jo that I will be late, keep it casual.
- Tell my roommate in the public group chat to empty the dishwasher, but be nice.
- I prefer short answers, so just say yes.
- Answer Mum's text and say I am fine.
- Write back politely, I can not come on Sunday.

Eli woke up to a loud beep. The TV was still on a news channel, and his head hurt. He reached for his phone and said, Call Mum. The assistant understood that he wanted to phone his mother, so it started the call. It rang four times and went to voicemail. Eli said, Leave a message, and the assistant recorded him saying, Hi Mum, call me back when you can. It was a quick message, but it was enough. Then Eli asked the assistant to turn on the speakerphone for the next call, and it did. A minute later, his mother called back, and they talked while he made tea.

Zoe was on the train with a silver suitcase and her phone. She typed fast: book a room for two nights in the beach town and tell me when check in is. The assistant understood two things: she wanted a hotel room for two nights, and she wanted to know the check-in time. It found a room near the water and said check-in was after three. Zoe told it to continue with the booking, and then she asked it to put a late arrival note on it, because her train came in at ten. The assistant did that. She smiled and turned back to the window. It was going to be a good day.

Grandma Ruth sat in her chair with a book. The lamp on her left was too bright. She said to the speaker, Excuse me, could you please make the lamp half as bright, because the light hurts my eyes when I read? The assistant understood that she wanted the lamp dimmer, so it set the brightness to fifty percent. Ruth said it was better, but could it be a little warmer. The assistant changed the color to a soft yellow. She felt she had earned a quiet evening after a day of chores. She read three chapters and fell asleep in her chair.

Making an appointment means choosing a time to see someone, like a hair stylist or a dentist. Each place has open hours, and you can only book inside them. When you ask for a haircut, you give a day and a time. People often change plans. They say, let me move it to Friday, or, make it an hour later. If they are running late, they say, tell the salon I will be ten minutes behind. Before the day, they might say, remind me the night before. To learn when a place is ready for customers, they ask, are you open on Sunday? Clear words help the booking go well.

Walt was not good with technology, and his computer made him nervous. His grandfather's old desk stood beside it. One morning the words on his screen looked too small, and he was in a hurry. He typed to the assistant: incrase the text size on my screen. The assistant understood what he meant, despite the typo, and increased the text size. Walt was pleased. He then asked it to remind him every week to save his files, and the assistant set a weekly reminder for Sunday at ten. Walt said thanks and went back to work, with the big letters easy to read.

name: water_plan
does: Tells you when and how much to water each plant in your garden.
inputs: the plants you have, where they sit, and the weather
people say:
- When should I water the herbs on the piano shelf?
- Is it too warm to water at noon?
- My basil is tasty but droopy, what does it need?
- How much water for the roses this week?
- Set the sprinkler to run early in the morning.

On a hot day, a fan or an air conditioner makes a room feel cooler. A fan moves the air, and air conditioning takes heat out of it. Even a waiter in a busy restaurant is glad to stand near the cold air. At home, people use them to sleep or work comfortably. The weird thing is that fans cool people, not rooms. People ask for changes in simple words: make it cooler, two degrees lower, turn the fan to low, or, cool the bedroom before I get home. Sometimes they just cheer when the air gets better, and say, that is perfect, hold it there.

Kai texted fast: ac on tomorrow at seven so my room is cool after my shower. The assistant understood that Kai wanted the air conditioning to start at seven tomorrow, so it made a schedule and said so. Kai's glasses always fogged when stepping from a hot shower into a warm room, and last night his sister had been angry because the whole apartment was hot. Kai also asked for the temperature to stay at twenty-two degrees. The assistant set that too. The next evening the room was cool and quiet, and nobody was angry at all.

Living near other people means sharing space, and sometimes things go bad. A storm knocks a branch onto the road. A dog barks all night. A colleague who lives nearby might say the noise kept them awake. People then use an app or a phone to ask for help. They say, tell the neighbors to stop the loud music after ten, or, post a note about the broken light. They change their mind with words like, never mind, or, wait until tomorrow. They also ask, who do I call about a fallen tree? Clear and polite words make neighbors happier.

A walk is easy to measure. Your phone counts steps, and it can turn the steps into distance. When you push a cart, or when the wind blows against you, the numbers can be a little off. People use these numbers to see whether they are close to a goal, like ten thousand steps a day. They ask, how many steps have I taken, or, how far did I go. If the number looks wrong, they say, that is not correct, I walked more than that, or, reset my steps for today. Some people also say, set my goal to eight thousand, to make it easier.

Homework is work for school that you do at home. Every subject has its own assignments, and each one has a due date. Students write them on a board, in a notebook, or on a phone. A short break helps the brain, and people often say, remind me to study for twenty minutes, then rest. When a due date moves, they say, change the math test to Friday, or, put the essay on Thursday. They also say, what homework do I have tonight? After a spicy lunch they might say, give me five more minutes. The right words help a student plan the week.

Gus the gardener wiped his forehead. It was a hot afternoon, and he wanted to drive to the garden center before it closed. He put on his sunglasses and said to his phone, How long to the garden center on Elm Street? The assistant understood that he wanted the drive time. It checked the traffic and said he would arrive in twenty-five minutes. Gus asked for the quickest way, and the assistant said to take the river road. It started the directions and read them out loud one turn at a time. Gus drove with the window open and came to the garden center ten minutes before closing.

Meal planning means deciding what to eat before you are hungry. Many families go through the week day by day: pasta on Monday, soup on Tuesday, and so on. A plan also helps with shopping, since you only buy what you need, like one ounce of cheese for each sandwich. People change the plan with simple words. They say, swap Tuesday and Wednesday, or, no meat on Friday, or, make dinner for six this week. Sometimes they ask, what can I make with eggs and rice? If they go out, they say, skip tonight, we are eating at a restaurant.

Lily was eight, and she was sitting at the kitchen table with her mom's tablet. She had a picture of a toy motorcycle in her head, a deep blue one. She said to the assistant, Find a blue toy motorcycle and print a picture of it for my wish list. The assistant understood two things: she wanted to see toy motorcycles for sale and she wanted a printed picture. It showed her three toys, and she pointed to the deep blue one. The assistant sent the picture to the printer, and a page came out. Lily taped it to the fridge, and her mom smiled when she saw it.
